findings.title: Unsanitized feed/remote HTML stored as raw_html post (stored XSS)
findings.body: Content from the RSS/Atom feed (`PollFeed`) or from a remote page (`import_remote`) is saved with `cook_method: raw_html`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` as-is, with no sanitizer. The embed view outputs it with `raw post.cooked`, and the normal Discourse topic view renders it too. Any `<script>`, `onerror=` or `javascript:` content in the feed therefore runs on the forum origin. A compromised or malicious feed, or a hijacked page on the embeddable host, gets full XSS against forum users, including admins. The HTML should be sanitized with a whitelist before it is stored.

findings.title: URL interpolated unescaped into HTML attribute
findings.body: `#{url}` builds raw HTML from the feed item's link/id without escaping. That HTML is then rendered unsanitized via the raw_html cook method. A URL containing a `'` breaks out of the href attribute and lets an attacker inject arbitrary markup or event handlers. `url` should be HTML-escaped (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`).

findings.title: Protocol-relative URLs are mangled by absolutize_urls
findings.body: Any href or src starting with '/' is treated as host-relative, including protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. The leading slashes are stripped and the embed host is prepended, producing `http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png`. This breaks every protocol-relative link and image in imported content. Values starting with '//' should be skipped or resolved properly, e.g. with `URI.join`.

findings.title: Crash on feed items without content / on Ruby < 2.1
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a `content` element. Many RSS feeds only provide `description`, so `content` is nil and the call raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole poll. Because `retry: false` is set, nothing after that item is imported. `String#scrub` also only exists in Ruby 2.1+, so on Ruby 2.0 this raises for every item. A fallback to `description` and a nil guard are needed.

findings.title: Every new embed URL triggers a full synchronous feed poll
findings.body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline whenever an embed URL is unknown. That fetches the whole feed over HTTP and runs import, including SHA comparisons and possible revisions, for every item. The only throttle is per URL. Any visitor hitting distinct article URLs (or the same URL with different query strings) on the embeddable host forces repeated full feed downloads and imports. There is no caching of the feed fetch (`feed_key` is defined but never used).

findings.title: `end if` typo turns following template output into the if-modifier condition
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` compiles to `end if` followed by the next generated `@output_buffer.safe_append=...` statement. Ruby parses that statement as the modifier condition, so the template only works by accident because the append is truthy and evaluated first, which reorders output. It should be `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: Nil post when embed's post was deleted
findings.body: `post = embed.post` can be nil if the post was hard-deleted, or not found because it was trashed via the default scope. `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises NoMethodError on every feed poll for that URL, breaking the import of all subsequent items.

findings.title: Substring-based origin check for postMessage
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl. For example, `https://forum.example.co` passes the check for `https://forum.example.com/`. The origin should be compared exactly against the parsed origin of discourseUrl.

findings.title: Editing an existing migration to add force: true
findings.body: Adding `force: true` to an already-shipped migration does nothing on installs that have already run it. On re-runs it silently drops the existing `top_topics` table. Changing historical migrations is unrelated to this feature and risky.
